insights.titulo: Founders' Table took the hours you planned for the Atlas Freight proposal
insights.por_que: Three of the five evenings went to demo-night logistics in WhatsApp with Sofia — venue, the team list, the food order. None of it was on the calendar, so the proposal block on Wednesday became the only proposal time all week, and it shrank to 70 minutes.

insights.titulo: Your big blocks only happen where the calendar already protects them
insights.por_que: The Northbeam build block after MKT 310 on Tuesday and Thursday, and Sunday night on Jarvis, are the stretches nobody books over. Mondays and Wednesdays break into pieces between CS 210, PHIL 120 and meetings; the longest free stretch on those days was 75 minutes.

insights.titulo: You answer Marco in twenty minutes and Dana in a day and a half
insights.por_que: Dana writes by mail, mostly before 9 a.m., and her two questions about the pilot scope sat until Thursday night. She is the person the week's first objective depends on; Marco can wait an hour without anything moving.

movida.que: Put two 90-minute Atlas Freight blocks on the calendar before Wednesday, and protect them like a class
movida.hacer: Finish the pilot proposal: scope, three metrics, price, a start date Dana can say yes to
movida.por_que: The proposal is the week's first objective and the only one with a deadline someone else sets. Last week it got 2.5 h; it needs about 3 h of uninterrupted work.

tarjetas.titulo: Do days with three or more meetings cost you your big blocks?
tarjetas.cita: If I have meetings I still get my deep work in, I just do it at night.

resultados.nombre: Minutes in blocks of 90+ on your fronts

ciencia.resumen: Studies of maker schedules find a single mid-afternoon meeting splits the day; output drops with the number of fragments, not the hours spent in meetings.

tarjetas.tu: On meeting-heavy days your big blocks drop to almost nothing, and the work shows up after 23:00 instead — the night shift you described is real, and it starts with the calendar.

tarjetas.titulo: Does a longer night give you more focused hours the next day?

resultados.nombre: Real hours on your fronts the next day
Minutes in blocks of 90+ the next day

ciencia.resumen: Sleep restriction below seven hours reliably lowers sustained attention within days, and people stop noticing the deficit after the first week.

tarjetas.tu: Longer nights lean toward more focused hours the next day, but with 16 paired days the gap is still inside what luck could make.

preguntas.texto: How rested do you feel right now?

tarjetas.titulo: Does a real midday break make your afternoons stronger?
tarjetas.cita: Lunch is a waste of time, I eat at my desk.

predictor.nombre: Longest break with no screen between 12:00 and 15:00

resultados.nombre: Real hours on your fronts after 15:00

ciencia.resumen: Short detached breaks restore attention for the following hours; breaks spent on a phone do not.

tarjetas.tu: Only 9 days have a break measured. It needs another two weeks before it can say anything.

tarjetas.titulo: When your Claude work on your fronts actually happens
tarjetas.cita: My best hours are late at night.

ciencia.resumen: Chronotype is real and partly genetic, but students drift later under social schedules; peak hours tend to move back after a week of earlier mornings.

tarjetas.tu: Two peaks: after the Tuesday/Thursday class at 14:00–16:00, and again at 22:00–00:00. The night peak is longer but split into short sessions.

tarjetas.titulo: Are you sharper at night? Your typing says no difference

ciencia.resumen: Typing errors rise with fatigue in lab tasks, but as a field signal they are noisy and depend on what you are typing.

tarjetas.tu: Same typo rate day and night across 13 days with both. The night is not sloppier — it is not sharper either.

ciencia.resumen: Completion clusters right before fixed deadlines and transitions; it measures closing, not the work itself.

tarjetas.tu: Most closes happen between 21:00 and 23:00 — the end-of-day sweep — and on Sunday evening before the weekly close.
